To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a maturity model can help organisations to develop a critical understanding of their Big Data maturity; and (ii) the proposed Big Data maturity model is considered to be complete, useful and applicable by both practitioners and researchers.

the maturity of an organisation’s Big Data initiatives can be assessed by evaluating the organisation on five dimensions (Big Data strategy, Big Data governance, Big Data architecture, Big Data analytics, and Big Data management) and 20 sub-dimensions.
the maturity model is a valuable instrument to assess the current state of an organization's Big Data capabilities and to identify improvement areas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to make the most of Big Data in organisations, not with how to manage Big Data.
how organisations can leverage Big Data and, thus, contributes to the understanding of the organisational aspects of Big Data.
the question of how organisations can realise the value of Big Data, and not with how to store and process Big Data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed maturity model is useful and applicable to organisations in their quest to appropriate value from Big Data.
the model is considered useful by practitioners and is applicable to real-world organisations.

the proposed maturity model is a valuable tool to help organisations to develop a critical understanding of their current Big Data capabilities and to identify the next steps to be taken to leverage Big Data for business value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the maturity model provides a framework for assessing the current state and for planning the next steps for the Big Data journey.
we developed a maturity model that supports organisations in their journey towards Big Data maturity and, in this way, enables them to realise the full value potential of Big Data.
the maturity model can be used to evaluate the maturity level of an organisation with regard to its Big Data strategy and to identify improvement opportunities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organisations should not only invest in Big Data capabilities but also in Big Data governance, as the two are complementary and necessary for the success of Big Data-enabled analytics initiatives.
organisations should not start a Big Data initiative without a clear understanding of their current Big Data maturity and the next steps to reach the desired maturity level.
the maturity of an organisation’s Big Data initiative should be assessed from a holistic perspective, considering both organisational and technological aspects.
